scope.current_boundary: Consolidates legacy lessons l05 and l06. Covers direction-based definition and comparison of transverse and longitudinal waves (oscillations perpendicular or parallel to energy transfer), physical identification of compressions and rarefactions in longitudinal waves, interpretation of displacement-distance and displacement-time graphs, deducing instantaneous particle motion direction from a travelling wave profile, and translating longitudinal waves to displacement graphs using displacement gradients. Strictly excludes wave intensity and amplitude-squared relationships (deferred to 9702_t07_cm04_l07), Doppler effect (deferred to 9702_t07_cm05_l09), electromagnetic spectrum wavelength ranges (deferred to 9702_t07_cm06_l11), full polarisation theory and Malus's law (deferred to 9702_t07_cm07_l13), and stationary waves/interference (deferred to Topic 8).
prior_scope_summaries_consulted: 9702_t07_cm01_l01: Progressive waves transfer energy without net transfer of matter through local oscillations about equilibrium positions.
9702_t07_cm01_l02: Wave quantities defined: displacement, amplitude, period, frequency, wavelength, wave speed, and phase difference.
9702_t07_cm02_l03: Determining amplitude and frequency with a CRO, and deriving and applying the progressive wave equation v = f lambda.
9702_t01: Vectors, scalar versus vector quantities, Cartesian coordinates, and right-angled resolution.

review_history.first_principles_check: PASS: Verified perpendicular vs parallel particle oscillations relative to energy propagation; verified compressions and rarefactions as density and pressure extrema with adjacent opposite separation lambda / 2; verified wave profile shift method for instantaneous particle velocity (rightward wave on rising slope moves downward; turning points at crests and troughs have zero velocity); verified longitudinal displacement gradient relationship (negative gradient at zero-crossing causes convergence into compression, positive gradient causes divergence into rarefaction, displacement peaks have zero gradient and normal equilibrium density); verified polarisation diagnostic test (transverse waves polarisable, longitudinal waves non-polarisable).
independent_recalculations: Worked Example 1: Plucked string particle oscillation perpendicular to energy transfer -> transverse wave confirmed.
Worked Example 2: Sound in air particle oscillation parallel to energy propagation -> longitudinal wave confirmed.
Worked Example 3: lambda = 2 * 0.19 m = 0.38 m; v = f * lambda = 16 * 10^3 Hz * 0.38 m = 6080 m s^-1 -> 6100 m s^-1 (2 s.f.) confirmed.
Worked Example 4: Graphical repeat intervals (distance -> lambda; time -> T); v = f lambda confirmed.
Worked Example 5: Rightward wave profile shift at rising zero-crossing -> vertically downwards particle motion confirmed.
Worked Example 6: Negative displacement gradient at downward zero-crossing A -> compression (maximum density/pressure); positive crest B -> normal equilibrium density/pressure confirmed.

unresolved.resolution: Strictly demarcated by scope boundary: this lesson plans and teaches progressive transverse and longitudinal wave definitions, compressions/rarefactions, and graphical interpretations. Intensity is owned by 9702_t07_cm04_l07; stationary waves and interference are owned by Topic 8 (9702_t08). In worked examples and activities, only the progressive wave classification and graph parts are taught.

unresolved.issue: Polarisation is introduced only as a diagnostic wave-type distinction without quantitative treatment
unresolved.impact: Students might expect coverage of polarising filters, transmission axes, or Malus's law calculations upon encountering polarisation.
unresolved.resolution: Strictly declared in scope boundary: polarisation is mentioned solely as qualitative physical evidence that a wave is transverse (since longitudinal oscillations cannot be polarised, as tested in 9702_s25_23_q05_a). Full treatment of polarisation, polarising filters, and Malus's law belongs to 9702_t07_cm07_l13.
